diagnosis.root_cause: Duplicate FreeRADIUS radcheck rows for the same username, including an orphan row with a conflicting line ID, cause authentication to resolve inconsistently and repeatedly disconnect the subscriber.
evidence: The subscriber has 19 sessions in 24 hours, exceeding the flapping threshold of 8, and the average session duration is only 38 minutes versus the 11.9-hour network mean.
RX power is stable in the normal band around -20.6 dBm, TX power is normal around 2.4 dBm, and both optical noise and TX bias remain stable.
Distance is constant at 96, so there is no fibre path change or distance-related fault.
All visible peers on EPON0/5 are online with normal optical levels, excluding a shared splitter, PON-port, or OLT fault.
The OLT, its metrics, router heartbeat, and VLAN 1055 are healthy and correctly provisioned.
RADIUS contains two rows for the same username; the orphan row has a different line ID and FreeRADIUS may resolve either row first.

Because the physical layer is clean and the authentication inconsistency directly explains the short, repeated sessions, the presenting fault is authentication session flapping rather than a signal fault or radius_lineid_conflict.

remediation.action: Remove the orphan radcheck row for username 30:16:9D:A2:5F:03, retain and verify the row mapped to line ID 00:A1:07:C4:1D:88, then force a single clean reauthentication and confirm stable session duration and consistent IP/line-ID attribution.

ground_truth.root_cause: Two radcheck rows exist for the same username. FreeRADIUS resolves inconsistently between them, so authentication succeeds or fails depending on which row is matched, producing repeated short sessions and two alternating IP assignments.
expected_reasoning: 19 sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline, with a 38 minute mean duration against an 11.9 hour norm
RX has been flat at -20.6 dBm for seven days inside the +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so signal is not the cause
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are all stable
Port neighbours are normal and the OLT is healthy, so no shared infrastructure fault
With no optical explanation available, the search moves to the authentication layer
RADIUS holds two radcheck rows for username 30:16:9D:A2:5F:03, one of them an orphan with a different lineid
Recent sessions alternate between two IP addresses, consistent with inconsistent row resolution
Traffic is erratic rather than declining, which fits intermittent authentication rather than a degrading link

expected_escalation.review_reason: Duplicate RADIUS rows must be resolved by hand; deleting the wrong row disconnects the customer

distractors: The session pattern is identical to signal-related flapping and invites that diagnosis
Zero-throughput windows in the speed series look like link loss but coincide with rejected auth
ONU is a Router type, inviting a CPE-fault explanation
